ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON WATER MANAGEMENT AND RESIDENT SUPPORT IN THE GEUM RIVER BASIN

Article 1 (Purpose)

The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Water Management and Resident Support in the Geum River Basin and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Types of Basic Environmental Facilities)

The term "facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 2, subparagraph 4 (f) of the Act on Water Management and Resident Support in the Geum River Basin (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following facilities established and operated by the State or a local government: <Amended on January 28, 2014; July 12, 2016; January 16, 2018>
1. Nonpoint pollution reduction facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 13 of the Water Environment Conservation Act;
1-2. Buffer storage facilities under Article 21-4 (1) of the Water Environment Conservation Act;
2. Artificial islands for growing aquatic plants, underwater air supply devices, algae removal facilities, algae reduction devices, and other facilities for preventing water pollution in rivers and lakes.

Article 3 (Consent of Residents for Designation of Riparian Zones)

(1) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to designate an area under the proviso to the introductory part of Article 4 (1) of the Act as a riparian zone, the Minister shall have the head of the Si/Gun having jurisdiction over the relevant area obtain the consent of residents in a manner that meets all of the following requirements: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Consent shall be obtained from at least two-thirds of the total number of owners of land and buildings within the relevant area;
2. Consent shall be obtained from owners of land constituting at least two-thirds of the total land area within the relevant area.
(2) The boundaries of rivers under Article 4 (1) of the Act shall be the boundaries of river areas under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the River Act and shall be determined following an on-site survey of the actual conditions of the relevant boundary lines, etc., in accordance with the following categories:
1. Rivers for which a management register for river facilities under Article 15 of the River Act (hereinafter referred to as the "management register") has been prepared and is kept: The boundary lines of river areas recorded in the management register;
2. Rivers for which no management register has been prepared and is kept:
(a) Rivers with embankments: The boundary lines of those embankments;
(b) Rivers without embankments: The boundary lines of river areas shown on topographical maps produced by the National Geographic Information Institute.

Article 4 (Areas Excluded from Riparian Zones)

(1) The term "areas prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 6 of the Act means natural settlement districts under Article 31 (2) 7 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. <Amended on July 28, 2026>
(2) The term "areas meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 7 of the Act means areas in which a natural village consisting of at least 10 households has formed.

Article 4-2 (Revocation of Designation of Riparian Zones)

(1) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to revoke the designation of a riparian zone pursuant to the main clause of the introductory part of Article 4 (3) of the Act, the Minister shall hear the opinions of the Geum River Basin Management Committee under Article 35 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee"). <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(2) Before hearing the opinions of the Committee pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall form a survey team consisting of officials of relevant central administrative agencies and the relevant local governments, experts, representatives of residents, etc. and conduct an on-site survey of actual conditions. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) When revoking the designation of a riparian zone, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may, where necessary, request the head of the competent local government to provide the following materials: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. The location and area of the area for which designation is to be revoked;
2. Topographical drawings showing the riparian zone before and after revocation;
3. Other materials that the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment deems necessary.

Article 5 (Procedures and Timing for Establishing Basic Management Plans for Riparian Zones)

(1) When establishing a basic management plan for riparian zones pursuant to Article 4-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "basic management plan"), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall, after hearing the opinions of relevant local governments, request deliberation by the Committee by August 31 of the year preceding the year in which the basic management plan must be established. <Amended on July 28, 2014; October 1, 2025>
(2) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to amend a basic management plan established pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister shall request deliberation by the Committee after hearing the opinions of relevant local governments: Provided, That this shall not apply where the Minister intends to amend minor matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment establishes or amends a basic management plan pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister shall notify the relevant local governments thereof. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 5-2 (Establishment and Implementation of Riparian Ecological Belt Implementation Plans)

(1) The term "matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4-3 (1) 4 of the Act means the following matters:
1. The current use of the target area;
2. Methods of purchasing the target area;
3. Management measures after development and analysis of the effects of the project;
4. Required financial resources and investment plans.
(2) The term "cases of amending minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 4-3 (3) of the Act means any of the following cases:
1. Changing the original size of the target area by not more than 30 percent;
2. Changing the development period by not more than six months;
3. Changing the originally required financial resources by not more than 30 percent.
(3) Pursuant to Article 4-3 (4) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall establish a riparian ecological belt implementation plan under the introductory part of Article 4-3 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "riparian ecological belt implementation plan") and request deliberation by the Committee by August 31 of the year preceding the year in which the riparian ecological belt development project must be implemented. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(4) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment establishes a riparian ecological belt implementation plan pursuant to paragraph (3), the Minister shall notify the relevant local governments thereof. The same shall apply where an established riparian ecological belt implementation plan is amended. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 5-3 (Scope of Manufacturing Businesses Excluded from Facilities Subject to Restrictions on Activities)

The term "manufacturing businesses prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as agricultural product processing businesses" in Article 5 (1) 8 of the Act means the manufacturing businesses specified in Annex 1.

Article 6 (Procedures for Permission for Activities in Riparian Zones)

A person who intends to obtain permission to install a facility under Article 5 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for permission, accompanied by the following documents, to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Installation specifications stating the area, structure, etc. of the facility to be installed;
2. Specifications stating the types of livestock, the number of livestock to be raised, and the method of treating livestock excreta (to be attached only where the applicant intends to install a facility under Article 5 (2) 2 of the Act);
3. Installation specifications and drawings for a sewage treatment facility under Article 24 (2) 1 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Sewerage Act (to be attached only where the applicant intends to install a facility under Article 5 (2) 3 of the Act).

Article 6-2 (Changes to Use Zones and Districts)

The term "special reasons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 5 (3) of the Act means cases in which it is necessary to expand a facility falling under any of the following subparagraphs (limited to expansions not exceeding 30 percent of the facility's original area):
1. Excreta treatment facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 11 of the Sewerage Act;
2. Public treatment facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 9 of the Act on the Management and Use of Livestock Excreta.

Article 7 (Water Quality Standards)

The term "standards prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 7 (1) of the Act means the standards for the following categories: <Amended on July 12, 2016>
1. Rivers: Biochemical oxygen demand of 1 milligram per liter or less;
2. Lakes: Total organic carbon of 2 milligrams per liter or less.

Article 8 (Procedures for Public Notice of Water Source Protection Areas)

Article 11 (2) through (4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to public notice of water source protection areas under Article 7 (3) of the Act. In such cases, "the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment" shall be construed as "Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, and Do Governors (hereinafter referred to as 'Mayors/Do Governors')". <Amended on July 28, 2014; October 1, 2025>

Article 9 (Procedures for Purchase of Land, etc.)

(1) A person who intends to sell land and facilities attached to such land (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc.") to the State pursuant to Article 8 (1) of the Act shall submit the following documents (including electronic documents) to the head of a river basin environmental office or the head of a regional environmental office: <Amended on May 4, 2010; November 2, 2010; July 28, 2014>
1. Deleted. <November 2, 2010>
2. Documents concerning the current use of the land;
3. Documents stating the details of structures on the land to be sold.
(2) The head of a river basin environmental office or the head of a regional environmental office who receives an application for purchase of land, etc. under paragraph (1) shall verify the following documents through the joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act: Provided, That where the applicant does not consent to verification of the document specified in subparagraph 1, the applicant shall be required to submit it. <Newly Inserted on November 2, 2010; January 8, 2019>
1. For an individual, an extract of the resident registration record containing the resident registration number;
2. For a corporation, a certificate of registered matters of the corporation;
3. A certified copy of the register of the land, etc. that the applicant intends to sell.
(3) The head of a river basin environmental office or the head of a regional environmental office who receives an application for purchase of land, etc. under paragraph (1) shall determine the priority for purchase in accordance with the criteria for purchase priority established by the Committee taking into account the characteristics of the Geum River basin, such as the distance from river boundaries and the extent of pollution loads, and shall notify the owner of the land, etc. of the purchase priority assigned to the relevant land, etc. <Amended on November 2, 2010>
(4) Deleted. <July 28, 2014>
(5) When purchasing land, etc. in an area falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 8 (2) of the Act, the head of a river basin environmental office or the head of a regional environmental office may give priority to purchasing such land, etc. following deliberation by the Committee. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 9-2 (Calculation of Purchase Prices for Land, etc.)

(1) The purchase price of land, etc. under the main clause of the introductory part of Article 8 (2) of the Act shall be calculated by taking the arithmetic mean of the amounts appraised by two or more appraisal corporations, etc. under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Act on Appraisal and Certified Appraisers pursuant to the main clause of the introductory part of Article 8 (2) of the Act. <Amended on August 31, 2016; March 9, 2021>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), the purchase price may be determined on the basis of compensation amounts for land, business losses, etc. under the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects in any of the following cases:
1. Where the case falls under Article 8 (2) 1 of the Act;
2. Where all of the land, etc. jointly offered for sale by several persons is purchased, and the land, etc. meets all of the following requirements:
(a) The land, etc. shall consist of at least two adjoining parcels with different owners;
(b) At least 50 percent of the area of each adjoining parcel of land, etc. shall lie within 200 meters of the boundary of a river or lake.

Article 10 (Target Water Quality for Each Section of the River System)

(1) When setting target water quality for each section of the river system under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall set such targets so that the water quality of major water sources can achieve and maintain a grade of "Slightly Good" or higher under subparagraph 3 (a) 2) and (b) 2) of Annex 1 to the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy. <Amended on July 20, 2012; October 1, 2025; July 28, 2026>
(2) A public notice under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act shall include the following matters:
1. The sections of the river system for which target water quality is to be set and the watersheds affecting those sections (hereinafter referred to as "watersheds");
2. Target water quality at the boundaries of Metropolitan Cities and Dos;
3. Target water quality for each section of the river system.
(3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall designate the downstream end of a watershed as the point for target water quality and measure and verify changes in the water quality of the relevant watershed, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 10-2 (Establishment of Target Water Quality for Areas of Jurisdiction)

(1) Before issuing a public notice under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall notify the Mayors/Do Governors of the deadline by which they may notify the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment of their intention to set target water quality for each section of the river system within their jurisdiction (hereinafter referred to as "jurisdictional target water quality") pursuant to the proviso to Article 9 (1) of the Act and the deadline by which they may apply to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for approval. <Amended on July 28, 2014; October 1, 2025>
(2) A Mayor/Do Governor who intends to give public notice of jurisdictional target water quality pursuant to the proviso to Article 9 (1) of the Act shall notify the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment of the intention to set jurisdictional target water quality within the notification deadline under paragraph (1), and shall then apply to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment for approval of the jurisdictional target water quality within the deadline for applying for approval under paragraph (1). <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) The criteria for approval under the proviso to Article 9 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. The jurisdictional target water quality shall be appropriately set so that the target water quality at the boundaries of Metropolitan Cities and Dos publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment pursuant to the proviso to Article 9 (1) of the Act can be achieved and maintained;
2. The jurisdictional target water quality shall be set on the basis of an appropriate analysis of any of the following matters:
(a) Matters concerning the current use of water and flow rates for each watershed;
(b) Matters concerning the current status, etc. of pollution sources associated with the watershed's natural geography and forecasts of pollution sources;
(c) Matters concerning the quantities of pollutants generated and discharged by each pollution source within the watershed, etc.;
(d) Matters concerning the relationship between water quality and pollution sources.
(4) A Mayor/Do Governor who obtains approval under the proviso to Article 9 (1) of the Act shall give public notice of the approved jurisdictional target water quality without delay.
(5) Where a Mayor/Do Governor who has notified the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment of the intention to set jurisdictional target water quality pursuant to paragraph (1) falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister shall set and publicly notify the target water quality for each section of the river system in the relevant area without delay: <Amended on October 1, 2025>
1. Where the Mayor/Do Governor fails to apply for approval within the deadline for applying for approval under paragraph (1), or fails to obtain approval even after applying;
2. Where the Mayor/Do Governor fails to give public notice under paragraph (4).

Article 10-3 (Areas Required to Establish Implementation Plans for Total Pollution Load Management)

The term "areas prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to the introductory part of Article 11 (1) of the Act means areas determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment from among special measures areas under Article 38 (1) of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 11 (Jurisdiction over Business Establishments)

The term "business establishments prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the first sentence of the introductory part of Article 12 (1) of the Act means the business establishments specified in Annex 1-2. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 12 (Methods and Criteria for Calculating Total Pollution Load Exceedance Surcharges)
(1) The methods for calculating benefits from excess discharges, imposition coefficients by exceedance rate, imposition coefficients by region, and imposition coefficients by number of violations under Article 13(3) of the Act, and the method for calculating the total pollution load exceedance surcharge under Article 13(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "total pollution load exceedance surcharge") shall be as specified in Annex 2. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) The number of violations under paragraph (1) shall be the number of times orders to take measures, suspend operations, or close facilities have been issued under Article 12(6) and (8) of the Act. In such cases, the number of violations shall be calculated for each place of business for the most recent two-year period, using the date on which the violation occurred as the reference date. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 13 (Notice of Payment of Total Pollution Load Exceedance Surcharges)
(1) Notice of payment of a total pollution load exceedance surcharge shall be given within 60 days from the date on which the grounds for its imposition arise. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) Notice of payment of a total pollution load exceedance surcharge shall be given in writing, stating the quantity of pollutants subject to imposition, the amount imposed, the payment period and place of payment, and other necessary matters. In such cases, the payment period for the total pollution load exceedance surcharge shall be 30 days from the date on which the payment notice is issued. <Amended on July 12, 2016>

Article 14 (Adjustment of Total Pollution Load Exceedance Surcharges)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or a Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, or head of a Si/Gun (hereinafter referred to as an "imposing authority") shall recalculate and adjust a total pollution load exceedance surcharge in any of the following cases, and, where the amount already paid differs from the adjusted amount, shall impose the difference again or refund it: <Amended on July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016; October 1, 2025>
1. Where the implementation of measures or compliance with orders has not been completed by the scheduled date for completing compliance with an order to take measures, suspend operations, or close facilities under Article 12(6) and (8) of the Act, or has been completed within that period, resulting in a change in the period of discharge of pollutants or discharged substances that serves as the basis for calculating the total pollution load exceedance surcharge;
2. Where, after a total pollution load exceedance surcharge has been imposed, a reinspection conducted upon a determination that the state of discharge of pollutants, etc. has changed from the time of the original measurement due to improvements to facilities, etc. reveals that the quantity of pollutants or discharged substances discharged differs from the quantity originally measured.
(2) Where a total pollution load exceedance surcharge is adjusted on the grounds specified in paragraph (1)1, the period of discharge of pollutants or discharged substances used to calculate the total pollution load exceedance surcharge shall be calculated to reflect the difference between the scheduled date of completion of compliance and the actual date of completion of compliance. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) Where a total pollution load exceedance surcharge is adjusted on the grounds specified in paragraph (1)2, it shall be calculated based on the remeasured quantity of pollutants or discharged substances discharged, limited to the period after the date of reinspection. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(4) The adjusted imposition or refund of a total pollution load exceedance surcharge under paragraph (1)1 shall be made within 30 days from the date on which it is confirmed whether improvements to the relevant discharge facilities or pollution prevention facilities have been completed, operations have been suspended, or closure has been completed. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(5) Where an imposing authority adjusts a total pollution load exceedance surcharge and imposes the difference again or refunds it, the imposing authority shall give written notice of the amount, the grounds, the place of payment or refund, and other necessary matters. <Amended on July 12, 2016>

Article 15 (Applications for Adjustment of Total Pollution Load Exceedance Surcharges)
(1) A business operator who has received a notice of payment of a total pollution load exceedance surcharge (hereinafter referred to as a "person liable for payment") may apply for adjustment of the relevant total pollution load exceedance surcharge where any of the grounds specified in the subparagraphs of Article 14(1) exists. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) An application for adjustment under paragraph (1) shall be made within 30 days from the date on which the notice of payment of the total pollution load exceedance surcharge is received. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) Where an application for adjustment is made, the imposing authority shall notify the applicant of the result of its processing within 30 days.

Article 16 (Extension of Payment Deadlines and Payment in Installments of Total Pollution Load Exceedance Surcharges)
(1) An imposing authority may extend the payment deadline for a total pollution load exceedance surcharge or allow payment in installments pursuant to the proviso to Article 29 of the General Act on Public Administration, and the same shall apply to amounts in arrears. In such cases, the extension of the payment deadline shall not exceed one year from the day following the payment deadline, and payment in installments shall be limited to no more than six installments within 12 months.
(2) Where the total pollution load exceedance surcharge payable by a person whose payment deadline has been extended or who is paying in installments under paragraph (1) exceeds twice the capital or total capital contributions of the person liable for payment (total assets in the case of an individual business operator), and it is deemed that the person cannot pay it even within the period under paragraph (1) because any of the grounds specified in the subparagraphs of Article 29 of the General Act on Public Administration continues to exist, the imposing authority may further extend the payment deadline or allow payment in installments.
(3) An extension of the payment deadline under paragraph (2) shall not exceed three years from the day following the payment deadline extended under paragraph (1), and payment in installments shall be limited to no more than 12 installments within 36 months.

Article 17 (Disbursement of Collection Costs)
(1) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall, pursuant to Article 13(7) of the Act, disburse to a Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, or head of a Si/Gun, as collection costs, an amount equivalent to 10 percent of the total pollution load exceedance surcharges and additional charges collected by that Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, or head of a Si/Gun (where adjusted under Article 14, the adjusted total pollution load exceedance surcharges and additional charges). <Amended on July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016; October 1, 2025>
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall settle each month the collection costs under paragraph (1) out of the total pollution load exceedance surcharges and additional charges paid into the Special Account for Environmental Improvement under Article 45 of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy, and shall pay them to the relevant Metropolitan City Mayor, Special Self-Governing City Mayor, or head of a Si/Gun by the following month. <Amended on July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016; March 9, 2021; October 1, 2025>

Article 18 (Scope of Buildings and Other Facilities for Which Permission, etc. Shall Not Be Granted in Cases of Noncompliance with Total Pollution Load Management)
"Buildings and other facilities of at least the size prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 16(1)4 of the Act means buildings and other facilities falling under any of the following subparagraphs: <Amended on May 9, 2014; July 12, 2016; January 16, 2018>
1. Facilities among Class 1 through Class 3 places of business under Annex 13 of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Environment Conservation Act whose planned project area falls under Annex 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act;
2. Facilities falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Seoul Metropolitan Area Readjustment Planning Act whose planned project area falls under Annex 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act;
3. Buildings and other facilities to which restrictions on activities do not apply pursuant to Article 18-2.

Article 18-2 (Exclusion from Application of Restrictions on Activities)
Where buildings and other facilities that discharge sewage under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Sewerage Act are installed within the jurisdiction of a Metropolitan City or Si/Gun that formulates and implements a total pollution load management implementation plan under Article 11 of the Act (excluding riparian zones under Article 4(1) of the Act), the restrictions on activities under Article 38(2) of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy shall not apply pursuant to Article 16-2 of the Act.

Article 18-3 (Expenses Necessary for Total Pollution Load Management)
"Expenses necessary for total pollution load management prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17 of the Act means the following expenses: <Amended on May 9, 2014; July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016>
1. Expenses necessary to formulate total pollution load management basic plans and total pollution load management implementation plans under Articles 10 and 11 of the Act;
2. Expenses necessary for evaluation under Article 11(4) of the Act.

Article 19 (Restrictions on Installation of Waste Landfill Facilities)
(1) "Distance prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 20 of the Act means the distance for each of the following categories:
1. Main stream of the Geum River: One kilometer from the boundary of the main stream of the Geum River;
2. Tributaries flowing directly into the main stream of the Geum River: 500 meters from the boundary of a tributary flowing directly into the main stream of the Geum River.
(2) Article 3(2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the boundaries of the main stream of the Geum River and its directly inflowing tributaries under paragraph (1).

Article 20 (Criteria for Areas Eligible for Resident Support Projects, etc.)
(1) "Criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 21(1)2 of the Act means the criteria for each of the following categories:
1. An area where the annual average biochemical oxygen demand previously exceeded 10 milligrams per liter: The annual average biochemical oxygen demand shall be no more than one-fifth of that before the residents' voluntary efforts or no more than 3.3 milligrams per liter;
2. An area where the annual average biochemical oxygen demand previously remained at no more than 10 milligrams per liter: The annual average biochemical oxygen demand shall be no more than one-third of that before the residents' voluntary efforts or no more than one milligram per liter.
(2) Where the heads of Si/Gun/Gu (the heads of Gu refer to the heads of autonomous Gus; hereinafter the same shall apply) deem that an area under Article 21(1)2 of the Act exists within their jurisdiction, they shall submit the following data concerning that area to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment by March 31 each year: <Amended on December 24, 2009; October 1, 2025>
1. Water quality data measured by any of the following testing institutions:
(a) The National Institute of Environmental Research and its affiliated institutions;
(b) Institutes of health and environment of Metropolitan Cities and Dos;
(c) River basin environmental offices and regional environmental offices;
(d) Offices of the Korea Environment Corporation under the Korea Environment Corporation Act;
(e) Other water quality testing institutions recognized by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment;
2. The area of the relevant region and the status of its residents;
3. Methods and details of water quality improvement;
4. Details of local residents' activities to improve water quality.

Article 21 (Scope of Eligibility for Resident Support Projects)
(1) The scope of residents or areas eligible for support under resident support projects pursuant to Article 21(1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on July 20, 2012; May 9, 2014; July 28, 2014>
1. Residents of a water source management area who have met all of the following requirements since before the designation of the water source management area, and the villages in which those residents reside:
(a) Have continuously been registered as residents of, and actually resided in, the Si/Gun/Gu (Gu means an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over a riparian zone under Article 4(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "riparian zone"), a water source protection area under Article 7(1) of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act and Article 7(1) of this Act (hereinafter referred to as a "water source protection area"), or a special measures area under Article 38 of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy (hereinafter referred to as a "special measures area") [including cases where a resident moved out of the relevant area for unavoidable reasons such as education, medical treatment, or official duties and moved back within six months (limited to one occasion)];
(b) Have continuously owned land, etc. in a riparian zone, water source protection area, or special measures area;
2. Residents who are spouses or lineal ascendants or descendants who have inherited, or received as a gift in its entirety, land, etc. that a resident falling under subparagraph 1 has continuously owned in the relevant area since before the designation of the riparian zone, water source protection area, or special measures area, and who have continuously been registered as residents of, and actually resided in, the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant riparian zone, water source protection area, or special measures area since before receiving the inheritance or gift [including cases where, after receiving the inheritance or gift, a resident moved out of the relevant area for unavoidable reasons such as education, medical treatment, or official duties and moved back within six months (limited to one occasion)], and the villages in which those residents reside;
3. Residents of a water source management area who do not fall under subparagraphs 1 and 2 and who have continuously resided in the relevant water source protection area since before its designation;
4. Residents of a water source management area who do not fall under subparagraphs 1 through 3 and who have continuously engaged in livelihoods determined by the Committee, such as agriculture, forestry, and fisheries, in the relevant water source protection area since before its designation;
5. Water source management areas and areas under Article 21(1)2 of the Act;
6. Areas of Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas under Article 21(1)3 of the Act.
(2) In applying paragraph (1)1 or 2, where land, etc. is jointly owned, only one of the owners shall be deemed the owner (meaning a person selected by agreement among the parties, or, where no agreement is reached, the owner with the largest share; where there are several owners with the largest share, meaning one person selected according to the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment). <Amended on May 9, 2014; October 1, 2025>

Article 22 (Criteria for Allocation of Support Funds, etc.)
(1) Resident support projects under Article 21(1) of the Act shall be classified into indirect support projects, direct support projects, and special support projects, and their details shall be as specified in Annex 3. <Amended on July 28, 2014>
(2) The criteria applicable to persons eligible for support under resident support projects pursuant to paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "persons eligible for resident support projects") and to each eligible area shall be as specified in Annex 4. <Amended on July 28, 2014>
(3) Financial resources provided for resident support projects (hereinafter referred to as "resident support project expenses") shall be classified into expenses used for indirect support projects and direct support projects (hereinafter referred to as "general support project expenses") and expenses used for special support projects (hereinafter referred to as "special support project expenses"). <Amended on July 28, 2014>
(4) The Committee shall determine the areas eligible for special support project expenses and the amounts of support, and allocate them, taking into account the extent to which resident convenience facilities and pollutant purification facilities have been installed, the status of renewable energy deployment, etc.; of the special support project expenses, expenses used for water quality improvement and regional development projects under subparagraph 3(b) of Annex 3 shall not exceed the amount calculated using the following formula. <Amended on July 28, 2026>

(Annual resident support project expenses - Expenses for installation and operation of renewable energy facilities under subparagraph 3(a) of Annex 3) × 30%

(5) General support project expenses shall be resident support project expenses excluding special support project expenses. Article 23 (Procedures for Implementing Resident Support Projects, etc.)
(1) To ensure the smooth implementation of resident support projects under Article 21 of the Act, the Committee shall notify the heads of Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over areas eligible for resident support projects of the following matters by March 31 each year: <Amended on March 9, 2021>
1. The amount of the following year's resident support project expenses to be provided from the Geum River Basin Management Fund under Article 31 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund");
2. Guidelines for formulating the following year's resident support project plan (hereinafter referred to as a "project plan").
(2) The heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall formulate a project plan including the following matters in accordance with the guidelines for formulating project plans under paragraph (1), obtain approval from the competent Mayor/Do Governor, and submit it to the Committee by April 30:
1. An implementation plan for the detailed contents of resident support projects specified in Annex 3;
2. Other matters specified in the guidelines for formulating project plans.
(3) When formulating a project plan under paragraph (2), the heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall collect residents' opinions in accordance with the procedures, methods, etc. prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu: Provided, That this shall not apply to a project for which the consent of the Si/Gun/Gu council has been obtained as prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu.
(4) The Committee shall deliberate on project plans taking into account the draft fund management plan under Article 66(5) of the National Finance Act and shall notify the heads of Si/Gun/Gu of the results without delay.
(5) Where the heads of Si/Gun/Gu intend to change important matters, such as the scale of a project or resident support project expenses, in a project plan that has undergone deliberation by the Committee, they shall obtain approval from the competent Mayor/Do Governor and undergo further deliberation by the Committee. In such cases, important changes requiring further deliberation by the Committee shall be specified in the guidelines for formulating project plans under paragraph (1).
(6) The heads of Si/Gun/Gu shall submit the results of implementation of resident support projects for each year to the Committee by March 31 of the following year.

Article 24 (Criteria for Support to Places of Business, etc.)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may give priority in providing technical and financial support under Article 22 of the Act to small and medium enterprise operators (meaning small and medium enterprise operators under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Act) who intend to improve any of the following facilities: <Amended on November 20, 2009; January 16, 2018; October 1, 2025>

Article 25 (Support for Operation of Water Pollution Prevention Facilities)
(1) The Committee may provide support of up to 30 percent of the operating costs of water pollution prevention facilities under Article 23 of the Act.
(2) A person seeking support under Article 23 of the Act shall apply to the Committee by March 31 of each year, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on October 1, 2025>

Article 26 (Notification, etc.)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, and heads of Si/Gun shall, when giving notice under Article 25(2) of the Act, do so by a document containing the main particulars of the project plan and a list of the land, etc. subject to use or expropriation. <Amended on July 12, 2016; October 1, 2025>

Article 27 (Scope of Public Waters Subject to Water Use Charges)
The term "public waters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 30(1) of the Act and the portion of paragraph (2) of that Article other than its subparagraphs means the following waters:
1. Dams in the Geum River basin whose stored water (貯水) is used as a regional water source under subparagraph 3 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act (based on the planned flood level line);
2. The main stream of the Geum River.

Article 28 (Submission of Materials)
(1) A water supply business operator shall, pursuant to Article 30(4) of the Act, submit materials containing the following matters to the Committee by the 15th day of the month following the month in which a notice of payment of the water use charge under Article 30(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "water use charge") was issued:
1. Quantity of raw water (原水) withdrawn;
2. Quantity of tap water supplied and the loss rate;
3. Materials for calculating the water use charge and payment details;
4. Other materials that the chairperson of the Committee requests upon deeming them necessary for calculating and forecasting water use charges.
(2) Where heads of Si/Gun approve the installation of private water supply systems or private industrial water supply systems under Articles 52 and 54 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act in waters under Article 27, they shall notify the Committee of that fact without delay.
(3) The head of the flood control office having jurisdiction over the Geum River basin shall notify the Committee without delay upon granting permission to use river water pursuant to Article 50 of the River Act.
(4) Where the Korea Water Resources Corporation under the Korea Water Resources Corporation Act enters into a contract with a local government to supply raw water drawn from public waters subject to water use charges under Article 27, either directly or after purification, it shall notify the Committee of the details of the contract without delay. <Newly Inserted on July 12, 2016>

Article 29 (Areas Exempt from Water Use Charges)
The term "areas prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 30(5) of the Act means the following areas:
1. Water source management areas;
2. Catchment areas of rivers flowing into dams used as regional water sources (meaning areas in which rainwater naturally flows into public waters, such as rivers and lakes, and which are enclosed by lines connecting the surrounding ridges).

Article 30 (Determination and Public Notice of Water Use Charge Rates)
(1) Every two years, the Committee shall deliberate on and adjust the rate of the water use charge, taking into account the financial resources required for the uses of the Fund under Article 33 of the Act.
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall give public notice of the rate of the water use charge deliberated on and adjusted under paragraph (1) no later than 90 days before the start of the fiscal year. <Amended on October 1, 2025>
(3) Where no public notice of the rate is given under paragraph (2), the most recently announced rate shall apply.

Article 31 (Method of Calculating Water Consumption by End Users)
(1) The quantity of water consumed by an end user under Article 30(1) of the Act shall be the quantity of water consumption used as the basis for assessing and collecting water service charges.
(2) Where a water supply business operator supplies a mixture of water from public waters subject to water use charges under Article 27 and water from other public waters, notwithstanding paragraph (1), the quantity of water consumed by end users in the water supply area under that operator's jurisdiction (meaning the jurisdiction of the local government where the operator is a local government) shall be the quantity calculated by multiplying the water consumption under subparagraph 1 by the proportion under subparagraph 2. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
1. The quantity of water consumption used as the basis for assessing and collecting water service charges;
2. The proportion of the operator's total water supply in the preceding year accounted for by the quantity of water from public waters subject to water use charges (meaning the planned quantity of water supply for the current year if there is no record of supplying water from such public waters in the preceding year).

Article 32 (Methods of Calculating, Assessing, and Collecting Water Use Charges for End Users, etc.)
(1) The water use charge for end users under Article 30(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "water use charge for end users") shall be calculated by multiplying the rate under Article 30 by the quantity of water consumption under Article 31.
(2) The water use charge for end users shall be assessed together with water service charges on the same payment notice and collected in cash or by credit cards, debit cards, or the like (hereinafter referred to as "credit cards, etc."). <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) A water supply business operator shall remit the water use charges assessed and collected from end users to the Fund without delay.
(4) Except as prescribed in this Decree, the specific methods of assessing and collecting water use charges for end users, collection procedures, and other related matters shall follow the procedures for collecting water service charges prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government. However, where the water supply business operator is not a local government, the procedures for collecting water service charges set out in the supply regulations under Article 38 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act shall apply.

Article 33 (Water Use Charges for Installers of Private Water Supply Systems and Users of River Water, etc.)
(1) Water use charges for installers of private water supply systems and users of river water under Article 30(2) of the Act shall be calculated by multiplying the quantity of water withdrawn by the relevant installer or user by the rate under Article 30. However, where the quantity of water withdrawn by an installer of a private water supply system is unknown, the charge shall be calculated on the basis of the average daily quantity of water supplied under subparagraph 3 of Article 58(2) of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act.
(2) Installers of private water supply systems and users of river water shall notify the Committee of the quantity of water withdrawn each month and the corresponding amount of the water use charge by the 10th day of the following month, and shall pay the charge into the Fund in cash or by credit cards, etc. by the last day of the following month. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) The Committee shall enter into an agreement with a credit card business operator under subparagraph 2-2 of Article 2 of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as a "payment processing agency") to enable payment of water use charges by credit cards, etc. <Newly Inserted on July 12, 2016>
(4) Where a water use charge is paid by credit cards, etc. under paragraph (2), the date of authorization by the payment processing agency shall be deemed the date of payment. <Newly Inserted on July 12, 2016>

Article 33-2 (Exemption of Users of River Water from Water Use Charges)
Where a user of river water under subparagraph 2 of Article 30(2) of the Act falls under any of the following, the water use charge shall be exempted pursuant to paragraph (7) of that Article: <Amended on January 16, 2018; March 9, 2021>
1. Where the State or a local government uses river water for the purpose of measuring water pollution;
2. Where river water is used for any of the following purposes, the water discharged into the river after use contains no newly added water pollutants under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Water Environment Conservation Act, and the quantity of water discharged is unchanged from the quantity of river water withdrawn:
(a) Where an electric power generation business operator under subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act uses river water as cooling water;
(b) Where river water is used to produce hydrothermal energy under Article 2(4) and subparagraph 5 of attached Table 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy.

Article 34 (Entrustment of Compulsory Collection)
A water supply business operator intending to entrust compulsory collection of water use charges pursuant to Article 30(9) of the Act shall send a document stating the following matters to the head of the local government to be entrusted with the collection:
1. Name and address of the person liable for payment;
2. Amount payable and payment deadline;
3. Whether a demand notice or a peremptory notice for payment has been issued, and the year, month, and day of its issuance;
4. Other necessary matters.

Article 35 (Uses of the Fund)
The term "projects or expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 14 of Article 33 of the Act means the following projects or expenses: <Amended on January 16, 2018; March 9, 2021; February 13, 2024>
1. Projects to create riparian green spaces;
2. Education and publicity for improving water quality;
3. Forestry projects to enhance water source recharge functions;
4. Management of water source management areas;
5. Environmental baseline survey projects;
6. Management of purchased land, etc.;
7. Projects to reduce nonpoint source pollution;
8. Costs of transporting and treating waste under Article 31(1) of the Water Environment Conservation Act (limited to those recognized by the Committee among local governments' shares of the costs for waste generated at dams designated by the Committee);
9. Water pollution prevention projects for groundwater development and use facilities that have no owner or administrator;
10. Projects to maintain and manage water intake and purification facilities among the water supply facilities under subparagraph 17 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
11. Projects to survey and research the current use of water resources, including river water;
12. Projects to survey the status of, and manage, leaked or abandoned livestock excreta, compost (堆肥), and liquid fertilizer (液肥);
13. Projects to prevent and reduce algal growth;
14. Other projects or expenses selected by the Committee for water management in the Geum River basin.

Article 36 (Operation and Management of the Fund)
(1) Where the Fund operation plan is finalized pursuant to Article 66 of the National Finance Act, the Committee shall notify the relevant local governments.
(2) The Committee shall review and evaluate the execution and use of Fund resources provided to local governments and other recipients, and reflect the results in the Fund operation plan for the following year.
